issues.description: Method Milkable.messageOnMilk(): Problem statement and UML specify messageOnMilk() should return a String (the text "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"). The template's Main prints the return value of messageOnMilk() (System.out.println(m.messageOnMilk())). In the solution repository, the Milkable interface declares messageOnMilk() with return type boolean, and Seal/Goat implementations print the milking message and return boolean true. This creates a concrete mismatch in the method return type and expected behavior that will confuse students: following the problem spec leads to a different signature than the solution, and callers in the template (Main) expect a String to print.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the interface and implementations match the problem statement: change Milkable.messageOnMilk() to return String, and update Seal and Goat to return the formatted string (e.g., "Seal Clarabelle is milked" / "Goat Buttinsky is milked") instead of printing and returning boolean. Ensure callers (Main and any tests) print the returned String. Alternatively, if the boolean-return-and-print design was intentional, update the problem statement and UML to specify a boolean return type and that implementations perform the printing; but prefer aligning the code to the current problem text (String return).
